checklist.step: Build the exam-file index from the Code of Conduct itself
actions: Download the current Insurance Code of Conduct (August 2022) and the BMA guidance notes from bma.bm and diff them against the copies filed at the last refresh.

Create one index row per Code section/sub-section (governance s.4-5, risk management s.6 including investment & ALM, outsourcing, business conduct s.8), each naming the artifact that evidences it, its owner and its refresh cadence.
Load the index as the top-level register in the compliance evidence repository under BMA Exam Readiness / <year>.
Circulate the index to each artifact owner and collect a written acknowledgement of ownership.
checklist.done: every Code section has an index row with a named artifact, owner and cadence, acknowledged in writing.

checklist.step: Stand up the exam-file folder structure with access controls
actions: In the compliance evidence repository create one folder per index section, named <section number>-<short title>, under BMA Exam Readiness / <year>.
Set permissions so artifact owners can write only their own section and the Market Conduct / Consumer Compliance Manager approves every upload.
Switch on version history so superseded artifacts are retained, not overwritten.
Record the folder map and permission matrix on the index cover sheet.
checklist.done: the folder tree mirrors the index, versioning is on, and the permission matrix is documented.

checklist.step: Collect the governance pack from the Corporate Secretary each quarter
actions: Request from the Corporate Secretary the quarter's board and risk-committee minutes, current committee charters and terms of reference, and the director register.
Export the signed minutes from the board portal as locked PDFs and file them into the governance section folder.
Check each minute set is signed/approved and note on the index row the meeting dates covered.
Chase any unsigned minute set with the Corporate Secretary before the quarterly refresh deadline.
checklist.done: the governance folder holds signed minutes and current charters for the quarter, and the index row shows the coverage dates.

checklist.step: File the board-approved investment policy and ALM framework as the s.6 pack
actions: Pull the current board-approved investment policy statement and ALM framework and confirm the board-approval date against the minutes in the governance folder.
Attach the latest quarterly ALM monitoring pack: duration and cash-flow matching positions versus limits, interest-rate stress results, and any limit-breach escalations with their dispositions.
Hand the pack to the Market Conduct / Consumer Compliance Manager with a one-page note stating the policy version, approval date and next review date.
File the set into the s.6 (Risk Management — investment & ALM) section folder and update the index row's currency date.
checklist.done: the s.6 folder holds the board-approved policy, the approval evidence and the latest monitored-limits pack with a stated next review date.

checklist.step: Collect the conduct-of-business evidence set
actions: Request from the Complaints Manager the complaints register extract for the quarter with root-cause codes and redress amounts.
Request from the Claims Director / Manager the claims-handling standards, current claims leakage/QA results and any fair-treatment breaches logged.
Request from the Chief Underwriting Officer the product-governance and sales-standards attestations for in-force Bermuda business.
File each extract into the s.8 business-conduct folder and record the as-at date on the index row.
checklist.done: the s.8 folder carries the quarter's complaints, claims-QA and sales-standards evidence, each with an as-at date.

checklist.step: Refresh procedure documents and annual attestations
actions: Run the GRC report of policies and procedures mapped to the Code sections and filter for review dates older than 12 months.
Send re-attestation tasks in the GRC platform to each document owner with a 20-business-day due date.
Replace superseded versions in the exam file with the re-approved versions, keeping the version history intact.
Escalate owners overdue by more than 10 business days to the Head of Compliance.
checklist.done: no procedure in the exam file has a review date older than 12 months and all attestation tasks are closed or escalated.

checklist.step: Maintain the BMA correspondence log
actions: Log every inbound BMA letter, email or information request the day it arrives, with the stated due date (default 10 business days when silent).
Attach the outbound response package and its transmittal sign-off to the same log entry when sent.
Cross-file both into the exam file's correspondence section so an examiner sees one complete thread per request.
Review open requests weekly and escalate any at T-2 days to the Head of Compliance.
checklist.done: every BMA request has a logged due date, a filed response thread, and nothing is open past due.

checklist.step: Run the monthly currency sweep across the index
actions: Export the index with each row's last-refreshed date and cadence from the GRC platform.
Flag every row past its cadence (quarterly rows older than 3 months, annual rows older than 12 months).
Open a GRC task against the artifact owner for each stale row with a 10-business-day cure date.
Report the stale count and aging to the Market Conduct / Consumer Compliance Manager by month-end.
checklist.done: the sweep report is issued and every stale row has an owned cure task.

checklist.step: Pre-assemble the first-day-letter response pack
actions: Build a standing pack answering the BMA's usual opening requests: corporate structure chart, board and committee composition, policy register, complaints summary, outsourcing register extract and the s.6 investment/ALM policy pack.
Store the pack as a single indexed bundle in the exam file with a cover memo template addressed to the BMA supervision team.
Refresh the bundle quarterly in the same cycle as the index refresh.
Have Regulatory Counsel pre-clear the cover memo template wording.
checklist.done: a counsel-cleared, quarterly-refreshed first-day-letter bundle exists and is retrievable as one package.

checklist.step: Run the annual retrieval drill against a mock first-day letter
actions: Draft a mock BMA first-day letter of 15 requests spanning governance, s.6 investment/ALM, conduct and outsourcing, without warning the artifact owners.
Start the clock and have the team assemble the response solely from the exam file — no new document creation allowed.
Record per-request retrieval time and completeness; anything not produced within 5 business days is a drill failure.
Debrief with the Head of Compliance and convert every failure into an index fix with an owner.
checklist.done: the drill record shows per-request timings, and every failure has an owned index fix.

checklist.step: Map exam findings from prior BMA reviews into the file
actions: File every prior BMA exam report, finding letter and the insurer's committed action plans into the prior-exams section.
Cross-reference each closed finding to its closure evidence and each open finding to its remediation record (feeds REG-054-C34).
Flag any artifact an examiner criticised previously so its refresh gets priority in the sweep.
checklist.done: prior exam reports, action plans and closure evidence are cross-referenced and criticised artifacts are flagged.

checklist.step: Brief the exam liaison protocol to executives
actions: Issue the one-page exam protocol: the Market Conduct / Consumer Compliance Manager is single point of contact, all BMA requests route through the correspondence log, and no ad-hoc document handovers to examiners.
Walk the CEO, CRO and CFO through the protocol annually and before any announced BMA visit.
File the briefing deck and attendance record in the exam file.
checklist.done: the protocol is issued, briefed with attendance recorded, and filed.

checklist.step: Log and cure exam-file gaps as compliance exceptions
actions: Raise a tracker issue for every gap found by the sweep, the drill or a live BMA request: what was missing, which Code section it evidences, and the exposure created.
Assign root cause (owner turnover, cadence too slow, artifact never existed) and a cure date.
Treat a missing s.6 investment/ALM policy artifact as a priority-1 issue escalated to the Chief Risk Officer the same day.
checklist.done: every gap has an issue with root cause, owner, cure date, and priority-1 items are escalated same-day.

checklist.step: Obtain Head of Compliance sign-off on the quarterly refresh
actions: Review the quarterly refresh summary: index coverage, stale-row count, open gaps and drill status.
Spot-check three index rows against the underlying folders before signing.
Sign the refresh certificate and file it as the quarter's readiness attestation.
checklist.done: a signed quarterly readiness certificate is on file with the spot-check noted.

checklist.step: Retain exam-file versions for the retention period
actions: Snapshot the exam file at each quarter-end and label the snapshot with the 10-year retention class.
Confirm superseded artifact versions remain retrievable through version history.
Verify the repository index makes each snapshot searchable by Code section and quarter.
checklist.done: quarter-end snapshots carry the 10-year retention label and are retrievable by section and quarter.

testing.step: Build the population of index entries and BMA requests
actions: Export the full exam-file index with owner, cadence and last-refreshed date per row from the compliance evidence repository.
Export the BMA correspondence log for the trailing 12 months with received and responded dates.
Reconcile the index row count to the repository folder count and resolve differences before sampling.
testing.done: both populations are extracted and the index reconciles to the folder structure.

testing.step: Reconcile the index to the Code of Conduct itself
actions: Take the current Insurance Code of Conduct from bma.bm and list its sections independently of the index.
Match each Code section to an index row; any uncovered section (especially s.6 investment/ALM and s.8 conduct) is an exception.
Check the index reflects any Code or guidance amendment issued in the period.
testing.done: every Code section maps to an index row or is listed as an exception.

testing.step: Draw a documented sample of index entries
actions: Select 100% of the s.6 investment/ALM rows and the prior-exam-finding rows.
Add 20 rows at random (seeded, reproducible) from the remainder, minimum 30 rows total.
Record seed, population size and selection date in the workpaper.
testing.done: a reproducible sample covering all s.6 and prior-finding rows is documented.

testing.step: Verify currency and completeness of each sampled artifact
actions: Open each sampled artifact and compare its as-at or approval date to the row's cadence.
Check the artifact actually evidences the mapped Code section rather than merely naming it.
List every stale, missing or mismatched artifact as an exception with its aging.
testing.done: each sampled row is marked current/stale/missing with evidence notes.

testing.step: Trace the investment/ALM policy to board approval
actions: Open the filed investment policy and ALM framework and read the version and approval date.
Locate the approving resolution in the board minutes on the board portal and confirm dates match.
Confirm the latest ALM monitoring pack shows positions against limits and that any breach carries a disposition.
A policy without traceable board approval is an automatic fail.
testing.done: the s.6 policy traces to a dated board resolution and the monitoring pack shows dispositioned limits.

testing.step: Test BMA request timeliness end-to-end
actions: For every BMA request in the period, compare the response sent date to the stated due date.
Verify each response package is filed with its counsel clearance and Head of Compliance transmittal sign-off.
List any late or unsigned response as an exception.
testing.done: every request shows on-time, cleared, signed responses or a logged exception.

testing.step: Re-perform a timed retrieval on five mock requests
actions: Draft five exam-style requests without notice, including one s.6 and one complaints-history request.
Time the team's retrieval from the exam file only, against the 5-business-day standard.
Compare results to the last annual drill and note any regression.
testing.done: five timed retrievals are recorded against the 5-day standard with regressions noted.

testing.step: Verify sweep and gap-cure discipline
actions: Check a monthly sweep report exists for each of the last 12 months.
Trace 10 stale-row flags to their GRC cure tasks and confirm closure within the 10-business-day standard.
Confirm any priority-1 (s.6) gap shows same-day CRO escalation.
testing.done: sweeps ran monthly and traced cure tasks closed on time with escalations evidenced.

testing.step: Log exceptions with root cause, owner and remediation date
actions: Raise one tracker issue per exception with the Code section affected and the exam-risk impact.
Assign root cause and an owner, and set a remediation date.
Carry every open exception into the next quarterly spot-check as a mandatory retest.
testing.done: every exception has an issue, root cause, owner, date and retest commitment.

testing.step: Conclude, sign and report the test
actions: Compute the currency rate against the ≥95% threshold and the BMA-response timeliness against 100%.
Write the conclusion (effective / effective with exceptions / ineffective) with evidence references.
Have the independent reviewer, who maintains no exam-file section, sign the workpaper.
Report results to the Head of Compliance and the audit committee, and file the workpaper under Compliance Testing / REG-054.
testing.done: a signed workpaper with thresholds computed, a stated conclusion and committee reporting exists in the repository.

checklist.step: Intake every BMA finding within 5 business days of the letter
actions: On receipt of a BMA exam report or requirements letter, register each individual finding as its own GRC record: finding text verbatim, BMA reference, Code section cited, severity as graded by the BMA, and any date stated in the letter.
Attach the letter PDF from the compliance evidence repository to each record.
Diarise any 14-day interim response deadline stated in the letter the same day.
Notify the Head of Compliance and the Chief Risk Officer of the new findings by end of the intake day.
checklist.done: every finding in the letter exists as a distinct GRC record with the letter attached and deadlines diarised, within 5 business days.

checklist.step: Grade severity and assign owners across the three lines of defence
actions: Grade each finding high/medium/low using the procedure's matrix (policyholder impact, prudential impact, repeat-finding status, BMA tone).

Assign a first-line action owner from the business area named in the finding, a second-line validator (Operational Risk Manager or Compliance), and flag high-severity findings for third-line closure by internal audit.
For cyber and resilience findings, mirror the 3LOD structure of the Cyber Code: operational management fixes, risk management validates, internal audit assures.
Record all three names on the GRC record.
checklist.done: each finding carries a severity grade and named first-, second- and (where high) third-line owners.

checklist.step: Draft the remediation plan with dated milestones
actions: With the first-line owner, break the fix into milestones each with a deliverable, an owner and a date; the final milestone is the closure-evidence package.
Pressure-test the end date against the BMA's expectation before committing it — a date you cannot hold is worse than a longer honest one.
Enter milestones into the GRC record and set T-30/T-14/T-5 reminders on the committed end date.
Have the accountable executive for the business area countersign the plan.
checklist.done: each finding has a milestone plan with a countersigned, committed end date loaded into GRC.

checklist.step: Send the committed response letter to the BMA
actions: Draft the response letter stating, per finding, the accepted root cause, the remediation plan summary and the committed completion date.
Where the BMA letter requested an interim reply, send it within 14 days of the initial notification even if the full plan is still forming.
Route the draft through Regulatory Counsel for clearance, then sign and send to the named BMA supervisor.
File the sent letter and delivery confirmation into the compliance evidence repository and link it to each GRC finding.
checklist.done: a counsel-cleared, signed response with committed dates is with the BMA inside the letter's deadline and filed against each finding.

checklist.step: Stand up the monthly remediation progress cycle
actions: Send a monthly GRC attestation task to every first-line action owner asking for milestone status, blockers and revised forecast.
Chase non-responders within 3 business days and escalate a second miss to the owner's executive.
Update each finding's RAG status and forecast date from the returns.
Publish the monthly remediation dashboard to the Head of Compliance and Chief Risk Officer.
checklist.done: monthly attestations are returned, RAG statuses updated, and the dashboard is issued.

checklist.step: Validate each completed fix in the second line before claiming it
actions: Re-perform or inspect the fixed control against the finding's original failure mode — do not accept the first line's word for it.
Check the fix addressed the root cause, not only the cited instance (a repaired report is not a repaired process).
Write a validation memo stating what was inspected, on what date, and the conclusion.
Return inadequate fixes to the first line with the gap named, and reset the milestone.
checklist.done: every completed fix carries a second-line validation memo or has been returned with a named gap.

checklist.step: Assemble the closure evidence pack
actions: Compile per finding: the original finding text, root cause, remediation actions taken, before/after evidence (screenshots, revised procedure versions, control outputs), and the second-line validation memo.
Name the pack <BMA reference>-<finding id>-closure and file it in the compliance evidence repository.
Link the pack to the GRC record so the log row resolves to evidence in one click.
checklist.done: a self-contained closure pack is filed and linked for every finding proposed for closure.

checklist.step: Obtain third-line sign-off on high-severity closures
actions: Internal audit independently tests the remediated control for high-severity findings, sampling live outputs where possible.
Confirm the closure pack would stand up to BMA re-inspection without supplementary explanation.
Sign the closure in GRC or return it with the deficiency named; a returned closure reopens the finding and its committed date.
checklist.done: every high-severity closure carries internal audit's dated sign-off; returns have reopened the GRC record.

checklist.step: Report closure to the BMA and request confirmation
actions: Send the BMA a closure letter per finding or batch, summarising actions taken and offering the evidence pack on request.
Ask the BMA to confirm the finding is closed or state what remains outstanding.
File the BMA's acknowledgement against the GRC record; the finding stays 'closed - pending BMA' until it arrives.
checklist.done: closure letters are sent, and each finding shows either BMA acknowledgement or a chased pending status.

checklist.step: Handle date slips through formal extension, never silence
actions: The moment a forecast passes the committed date, log an exception in the tracker with the cause and the new forecast.
Have the Head of Compliance write to the BMA before the committed date passes, explaining the slip and proposing a revised date.
Record the BMA's response; only a BMA-acknowledged extension changes the committed date in GRC.
Report every slip, agreed or not, to the risk committee at its next sitting.
checklist.done: no committed date passes silently — every slip shows a pre-deadline BMA letter and a logged disposition.

checklist.step: Escalate overdue and repeat findings
actions: Review the aging report monthly; any action overdue against its BMA-committed date goes to the Chief Risk Officer and the accountable executive within 2 business days.
Tag repeat findings (same root cause as a prior exam) and brief the CEO, since repeats drive BMA supervisory escalation.
Minute the escalation decisions and file them with the finding.
checklist.done: overdue items show a dated CRO escalation and repeats show a CEO briefing, both minuted.

checklist.step: Report the remediation portfolio to the risk committee
actions: Prepare the quarterly paper: findings opened/closed, aging against committed dates, slips and extensions, repeat-finding analysis.
Publish through the board portal for the risk committee pack.
Capture the committee's challenge and directions in the minutes and feed them back into the plans.
checklist.done: the quarterly paper is in the committee pack and directions are minuted and actioned.

checklist.step: Keep the remediation log regulator-ready
actions: Maintain the log export format the BMA sees: finding, BMA reference, severity, owner, committed date, status, closure evidence link.
Test the export quarterly and fix any broken evidence links.
Ensure the export is producible within 5 business days of a BMA request.
checklist.done: a clean, link-verified log export is producible on 5 business days' notice.

checklist.step: Retain the full remediation record
actions: Apply the 10-year retention label to finding letters, plans, progress reports, closure packs and BMA acknowledgements at closure.
Verify retrieval by BMA reference and finding id in the repository index.
Confirm reopened findings retain their full prior history.
checklist.done: closed findings carry the 10-year label and retrieve by BMA reference with history intact.

checklist.step: Run the annual lessons-learned review
actions: Analyse the year's findings by root cause, business area and line of defence that should have caught them first.
Feed systemic causes into the compliance monitoring plan and the internal audit universe.
Present the analysis to the risk committee with proposed control investments.
checklist.done: an annual root-cause analysis is presented and monitoring/audit plans reflect it.

testing.step: Build the population of findings from source letters, not the log
actions: Pull every BMA exam report and requirements letter received in the trailing 12 months from the correspondence files.
List each individual finding directly from the letters to form the independent population.
Extract the GRC remediation log for the same period.
testing.done: an independent letter-derived finding list and the GRC log extract both exist in the workpaper.

testing.step: Reconcile the log to the letters
actions: Match every letter-derived finding to a GRC record; an unlogged finding is an automatic exception.
Check each record was created within 5 business days of the letter date.
Check the committed date in GRC matches the date in the signed BMA response letter.
testing.done: every finding matches a timely GRC record with a letter-consistent committed date, or is excepted.

testing.step: Draw the sample
actions: Take 100% of high-severity findings, 100% of findings with slipped dates, and all repeat findings.
Add a random, seeded selection from the remainder to reach at least 20 findings or the full population if smaller.
Record seed, population size and selection date.
testing.done: a reproducible sample covering all high-severity, slipped and repeat findings is documented.

testing.step: Recompute deadline maths per sampled finding
actions: Recompute the 14-day interim-response deadline from the letter date and compare to the actual sent date on the filed response.
Compare actual completion dates to committed dates and flag any overrun.
For extensions, confirm the BMA letter proposing the new date pre-dates the original committed date.
testing.done: all deadline recomputations reconcile or the variance is listed as an exception.

testing.step: Re-perform closure validation on sampled fixes
actions: For each sampled closed finding, open the closure pack and independently re-test the remediated control against the original failure mode.
Judge whether the fix addresses root cause or only the cited instance.
Any closure that fails re-performance is an exception and a candidate for reopening.
testing.done: each sampled closure has an independent re-performance note with a pass/fail call.

testing.step: Verify the 3LOD sign-off chain
actions: Check each sampled closure carries the second-line validation memo and, for high severity, the Chief Audit Executive's dated sign-off.
Confirm the signer is segregated from the action owner on every record.
Flag any self-validated closure as an exception regardless of outcome.
testing.done: every sampled closure shows a segregated, complete sign-off chain.

testing.step: Trace BMA communications end-to-end
actions: For sampled findings, trace response letter, any extension letters, closure letter and BMA acknowledgement in the repository.
Confirm counsel clearance and Head of Compliance signature on each outbound letter.
List any closure claimed internally but never reported to the BMA.
testing.done: the full BMA correspondence chain is evidenced for every sampled finding.

testing.step: Test escalation and committee reporting
actions: Check overdue items in the period show CRO escalation within 2 business days.
Verify quarterly remediation papers reached the risk committee and directions were minuted.
Confirm repeat findings were briefed to the CEO as required.
testing.done: escalations, committee papers and repeat-finding briefings are evidenced for the period.

testing.step: Log exceptions with root cause, owner and remediation date
actions: Raise one tracker issue per exception with the finding id, what failed and the regulatory exposure.
Assign root cause (intake miss, optimistic dating, weak validation) and an owner with a cure date.
Mark any silently missed BMA date for disclosure assessment with Regulatory Counsel.
testing.done: every exception carries an issue, root cause, owner, cure date and, where needed, a disclosure assessment.

testing.step: Conclude, sign and report the test
actions: Compute performance against the thresholds: 100% timely intake, zero unagreed date misses, 100% evidenced closures.
Write the conclusion with evidence references and the exception schedule.
Have the independent reviewer, who owned no sampled action, sign the workpaper.
Report to the audit committee and file the workpaper under Compliance Testing / REG-054.
testing.done: a signed workpaper with a stated conclusion and committee reporting is filed.

checklist.step: Refresh the business impact analysis annually
actions: Issue the BIA questionnaire in the GRC platform to every department head, asking for their processes, peak periods, tolerable downtime, workaround capacity and upstream dependencies.
Interview the Claims Director / Manager, Policy Admin Ops Lead, Billing Operations Manager and Treasury Manager to pressure-test the answers where policyholder money moves.
Score each process for policyholder impact, financial impact and regulatory impact, and mark critical those the insurer cannot suspend beyond its stated tolerance.
Publish the refreshed BIA and have the Operational Risk Manager countersign the criticality list.
checklist.done: a countersigned BIA dated within 12 months names every critical process with its tolerable downtime.

checklist.step: Set RTO/RPO per critical process and its applications
actions: For each critical process, set the recovery time objective from the BIA's tolerable downtime and a recovery point objective from data-loss tolerance.
Map the process to its applications in the CMDB and record the RTO/RPO on each application record.
Ask the Disaster Recovery Manager to confirm in writing that the current DR architecture can meet each RTO/RPO, and log every shortfall as a risk acceptance or an investment action.
Reconcile the application list against the critical third-party register (REG-054-C37) so outsourced services carry the same objectives.
checklist.done: every critical process and application carries an RTO/RPO, with DR feasibility confirmed or the gap formally logged.

checklist.step: Maintain the enterprise BCP document
actions: Update the enterprise BCP with the refreshed BIA, the crisis-management structure, invocation criteria and authority chain, alternate-site and remote-work arrangements, and communication trees.
Include the policyholder-fairness provisions the Code expects: how claims payments, policy service and complaint handling continue during disruption.
Version the document in the repository and record the change summary in the front matter.
checklist.done: the enterprise BCP reflects the current BIA and names how policyholder-facing operations continue, with a versioned change summary.

checklist.step: Maintain departmental continuity plans for every critical process
actions: For each critical process, keep a departmental plan naming the recovery team, call tree, first-24-hours actions, manual workarounds and minimum staffing.
Register every plan on the GRC plan register with owner, version and approval date.
Flag on the register any critical process from the BIA that lacks a plan — that flag is a priority exception, not a to-do.
checklist.done: the plan register shows an owned, versioned, approved plan for every critical process, with zero unflagged gaps.

checklist.step: Maintain DR runbooks for critical applications
actions: Keep a runbook per critical application: failover steps, restore-from-backup steps, data-validation queries, rollback criteria and the named engineers authorised to execute.
Store runbooks in the ITSM knowledge base linked from the application's CMDB record.
Update the runbook within 30 days of any material infrastructure change, confirmed via the change-management feed.
Verify backup schedules actually support the stated RPO for each application.
checklist.done: every critical application has a current runbook linked in the CMDB and a backup schedule consistent with its RPO.

checklist.step: Run the annual plan review cycle on the anniversary schedule
actions: Open a GRC review task per plan at T-60 days before its approval anniversary.
Require each plan owner to re-verify call trees, staffing, workarounds and dependencies against current reality, not last year's plan.
Collect the owner's dated review attestation and the executive's re-approval in the GRC record.
Close the cycle before the annual test window so tests exercise current plans.
checklist.done: every plan carries an owner attestation and executive re-approval dated within 12 months, before the test window opens.

checklist.step: Fold in Code and guidance changes
actions: At each annual cycle, re-read the Insurance Code of Conduct s.6/s.8 and the BMA Operational Resilience and Outsourcing Guidance Notes (2025) against the BCM framework.
Log each new expectation (impact tolerances, important business services, third-party dependencies) as a plan-change requirement with an owner.
Confirm the Business Continuity Manager closes each requirement before the board approval step.
checklist.done: a documented regulatory-delta review exists and every identified change is closed into the plans.

checklist.step: Update plans within 30 days of any incident or test debrief
actions: Take the lessons-learned actions from every invocation, near-miss and test debrief (REG-054-C36) into the GRC action log.
Amend the affected plan sections and increment the version within 30 days of the debrief.
Note in the plan's change summary which incident or test drove each amendment.
checklist.done: every debrief action is reflected in an amended plan version within 30 days, with traceable change notes.

checklist.step: Keep out-of-band copies usable during an outage
actions: Refresh the offline plan set (encrypted USB or printed crisis packs plus the mass-notification tool's document store) at every version change.
Verify the crisis team can open the out-of-band copies without corporate network access, twice a year.
Log the refresh date on the plan register.
checklist.done: out-of-band copies match the current versions and their accessibility check is logged.

checklist.step: Verify contact and call-tree data quarterly
actions: Extract joiners/movers/leavers from HR each quarter and update recovery-team rosters and call trees.
Run a silent call-tree notification test for one department per quarter and record response rates.
Correct dead contacts within 5 business days of the test.
checklist.done: rosters reconcile to HR data, and the quarterly call-tree test result is logged with corrections applied.

checklist.step: Present the plan set to the board risk committee annually
actions: Prepare the annual BCM paper: BIA summary, plan-register status, RTO/RPO shortfalls with risk acceptances, test results and investment asks.
Table the enterprise BCP for re-approval through the board portal.
Minute the approval and file the minute reference on the plan register — this is the Code's 'approved BCP' evidence.
checklist.done: the board risk committee's re-approval of the enterprise BCP is minuted and referenced on the register.

checklist.step: Wire continuity duties into outsourced-service contracts
actions: For each critical outsourced service on the third-party register, confirm the contract obliges the provider to maintain and test its own BCP and to evidence it annually.
Collect the provider's latest BCP attestation or test summary and file it against the vendor record.
Log any provider unable to evidence continuity as a register exception feeding REG-054-C37.
checklist.done: every critical provider shows a contractual continuity duty and a current attestation, or a logged exception.

checklist.step: Train recovery teams on their plan roles
actions: Assign the annual BCM module in the learning management system to every named recovery-team member and crisis-team alternate.
Run a tabletop walkthrough for new recovery-team members within 60 days of appointment.
Report completion to the Business Continuity Manager and chase non-completers past 30 days.
checklist.done: LMS records show current training for all named recovery roles, with new joiners walked through within 60 days.

checklist.step: Log and cure plan-coverage exceptions
actions: Raise a tracker issue for every uncovered critical process, overdue review, RTO/RPO shortfall or stale out-of-band copy.
Assign root cause and an owner with a cure date proportionate to the exposure.
Route closure of coverage gaps to the Chief Risk Officer for sign-off.
checklist.done: every exception carries an issue, owner and cure date, with CRO sign-off on coverage-gap closures.

checklist.step: Retain plan history and approvals
actions: File superseded plan versions, BIA outputs, attestations and approval minutes into the compliance evidence repository at each annual cycle.
Apply the 10-year retention label and verify retrieval by plan name and year.
Keep the mapping between plan versions and the test cycles that exercised them.
checklist.done: the historical plan record is retained 10 years and each version maps to its test evidence.

testing.step: Build the population from the BIA, the plan register and the CMDB
actions: Export the critical-process list from the current BIA, the full plan register from the GRC platform, and the critical-application list from the CMDB.
Reconcile the three: every critical process should map to a plan and every critical application to a runbook and RTO/RPO.
Resolve extraction differences before sampling.
testing.done: a three-way reconciled population of processes, plans and applications exists in the workpaper.

testing.step: Test coverage — no critical process without an approved plan
actions: Match each BIA-critical process to a registered plan with an executive approval date.
List every unmatched process as an automatic exception.
Check the enterprise BCP itself carries a board risk-committee approval minute dated within 12 months.
testing.done: coverage is 100% or exceptions are listed, and the board approval minute is verified.

testing.step: Draw a documented sample of plans
actions: Select the enterprise BCP, all plans covering claims payment, policy administration and treasury, plus a seeded random selection to reach at least 12 plans.
Include at least one plan whose owner changed during the year, since owner turnover is the commonest currency failure.
Record seed, population and selection date so the sample can be re-drawn.
testing.done: a reproducible sample including all policyholder-money plans is documented.

testing.step: Verify review currency on each sampled plan
actions: Compare each sampled plan's owner attestation and re-approval dates to its prior approval anniversary.
Confirm the review preceded the annual test window.
Flag any plan reviewed by simple re-dating without substantive change where the change-management feed shows material environment changes.
testing.done: each sampled plan shows a genuine review within 12 months or is excepted.

testing.step: Re-perform content checks against current reality
actions: Call three names from a sampled call tree and confirm they hold the stated role and know their recovery duties.
Trace two named workarounds to the teams that would execute them and confirm they are still feasible.
Check the plan's dependencies against the current CMDB mapping, not last year's.
testing.done: sampled call trees, workarounds and dependencies verify against current staff and systems.

testing.step: Recompute RTO/RPO consistency
actions: For sampled critical applications, compare the CMDB RTO/RPO to the BIA tolerable downtime and to the backup schedule actually configured.
Recompute whether backup frequency can mathematically meet the stated RPO.
Any critical application with unset or inconsistent objectives is an automatic fail.
testing.done: RTO/RPO values reconcile across BIA, CMDB and backup configuration for every sampled application.

testing.step: Trace post-incident and post-test updates
actions: Take the period's invocation and test debriefs and trace each action into an amended plan version.
Recompute the 30-day update clock from debrief date to version date.
List untraced actions or late updates as exceptions.
testing.done: every debrief action traces to a timely plan amendment or an exception.

testing.step: Test out-of-band accessibility without the network
actions: With the Business Continuity Manager observing, open the out-of-band plan copies from a device with corporate network access disabled.
Confirm the versions match the current register versions.
Record timing and any access failure.
testing.done: out-of-band copies open network-free and match current versions, with the result recorded.

testing.step: Log exceptions with root cause, owner and remediation date
actions: Raise one tracker issue per exception naming the process or plan, the gap and the disruption exposure.
Assign root cause (BIA drift, owner turnover, review theatre) and an owner with a cure date.
Carry open exceptions into next year's test as mandatory retests.
testing.done: every exception has an issue, root cause, owner, cure date and retest commitment.

testing.step: Conclude, sign and report the test
actions: Compute results against the thresholds: 100% coverage, 100% review currency, zero unset RTO/RPO on critical applications.
Write the conclusion (effective / effective with exceptions / ineffective) with evidence references.
Have the independent reviewer, who authored no sampled plan, sign the workpaper.
Report to the risk committee alongside the annual BCM paper and file the workpaper under Compliance Testing / REG-054.
testing.done: a signed workpaper with a stated conclusion and committee reporting is filed in the repository.

checklist.step: Build the annual test calendar from the service and application inventory
actions: Pull the important-business-service list from the BIA (REG-054-C35) and the critical-application list with RTO/RPO from the CMDB.
Schedule at least one scenario test per service and one DR test per critical application inside the calendar year, avoiding quarter-end financial close and peak renewal windows.
Load the calendar as scheduled ITSM tasks with named test leads and T-45-day preparation triggers.
Present the calendar to the risk committee for noting and file the minute reference.
checklist.done: a committee-noted calendar covers every service and critical application with owned, scheduled ITSM tasks.

checklist.step: Design severe-but-plausible scenarios per the BMA guidance
actions: Draft scenarios that stress each service to its impact tolerance: data-centre loss, ransomware with backup encryption attempted, loss of a critical third party (tie to the REG-054-C37 register), and sustained staff unavailability.
Define per scenario the disruption injected, the impact tolerance being tested (e.g. claims payments resume within X hours), and the pass condition.
Have the Operational Risk Manager challenge severity — a scenario the firm is certain to pass is redesigned.
Include at least one unannounced component agreed privately with the Chief Information Officer.
checklist.done: each service has a documented, risk-challenged scenario with an explicit impact tolerance and pass condition.

checklist.step: Prepare each DR test with a controlled runsheet
actions: Write the runsheet from the application's DR runbook: failover steps, data-validation queries, rollback criteria, abort authority and the timing checkpoints to capture.
Book the change window through ITSM change management and notify affected business owners 10 business days ahead.
Confirm backups completed cleanly in the 24 hours before the test so RPO measurement is honest.
Brief the named engineers and the observer who will independently record timings.
checklist.done: an approved change window, a runsheet with checkpoints, verified fresh backups and a named observer exist per test.

checklist.step: Execute DR failovers and capture timings verbatim
actions: Execute the runsheet: declare the simulated loss, fail the application over to the recovery site or region, and start the clock at declaration.
Record each checkpoint time in the ITSM test record as it happens — no retrospective reconstruction.
Run the data-validation queries and record the measured data-loss window against the RPO.
Have the business owner execute a real transaction on the recovered system (e.g. a claims payment in the Claims Platform) and capture the evidence.
Fail back per the runsheet and confirm production integrity before closing the window.
checklist.done: the ITSM record holds contemporaneous timings, an RPO measurement, business transaction evidence and a clean failback.

checklist.step: Run the scenario exercises with the crisis team
actions: Facilitate each scenario as a live exercise: inject the disruption, let the crisis team invoke the BCP and work the timeline against the impact tolerance.
Script injects that force real decisions — regulator notification (feeds REG-054-C38), customer communications, third-party escalation.
Have a scribe log decisions, timings and points of confusion verbatim.
Compare the achieved recovery to the stated impact tolerance and record the result as within/outside tolerance.
checklist.done: each scenario has a scribe log, a timeline, and an explicit within/outside-tolerance conclusion.

checklist.step: Test third-party-dependent services with the provider
actions: For services running on critical providers, obtain the provider's participation in the failover test or their own current test evidence under the contract clause.
Exercise the provider-loss scenario: operate the service on the documented workaround for the tolerance period.
File the provider evidence against the vendor record and flag any provider refusing to evidence testing as a register exception.
checklist.done: every third-party-dependent service shows joint-test participation or current provider evidence, with refusals excepted.

checklist.step: Grade every result against RTO/RPO and impact tolerance
actions: Compare measured recovery time to the application RTO and measured data loss to the RPO, and mark each test pass/fail in the ITSM record.
Mark each scenario within/outside impact tolerance from the exercise log.
Never re-grade a fail as a pass because the miss was small — log the variance and let remediation decide.
checklist.done: every test carries an evidence-backed pass/fail grade with variances logged, not rationalised.

checklist.step: Hold the debrief within 10 business days of each test
actions: Convene test lead, engineers, business owner and observer; walk the timeline and extract what broke, what was slow and what was luck.
Write the debrief note: result, vulnerabilities found, and candidate remediations.
Circulate to the Chief Information Officer and Operational Risk Manager.
checklist.done: a circulated debrief note exists within 10 business days of each test.

checklist.step: Issue the remediation plan within 30 days of each debrief
actions: Convert every vulnerability into an ITSM action with an owner, a date and a severity tied to the tolerance breached.
Route impact-tolerance breaches to the Chief Risk Officer for acceptance or funding decisions.
Schedule a retest for any failed application inside 90 days.
Publish the consolidated remediation plan within 30 days of the debrief.
checklist.done: a dated remediation plan with owners exists within 30 days, breaches are CRO-routed and failed tests have 90-day retests.

checklist.step: Track remediation to closure with evidence
actions: Review open actions weekly and chase owners at T-5 days.
Require closure evidence (config change record, updated runbook version, retest result) on every action before closing it.
Obtain CIO sign-off on ICT vulnerability closures and CRO sign-off on tolerance-breach closures.
Report aging monthly to the Operational Risk Manager.
checklist.done: every action closes with evidence and the required sign-off, and aging is reported monthly.

checklist.step: Feed results back into plans and runbooks
actions: Update DR runbooks and continuity plans (REG-054-C35) with every step that proved wrong or missing, within the 30-day update window.
Correct CMDB RTO/RPO entries where testing proved them unachievable and route the gap as a formal risk decision.
Note the driving test id in each document's change summary.
checklist.done: runbooks, plans and CMDB objectives reflect test findings with traceable change notes.

checklist.step: Report the programme to the risk committee and board
actions: Prepare the annual resilience-testing paper: calendar completion, pass rates, tolerance breaches, remediation aging and next year's focus.
Table it at the risk committee via the board portal and capture directions in the minutes.
File the paper and minute in the compliance evidence repository as the Code's annual-testing evidence.
checklist.done: the annual paper is tabled, minuted and filed as evidence of at-least-annual testing.

checklist.step: Log calendar misses and tolerance breaches as exceptions
actions: Raise a tracker issue for any service or application that misses its annual test slot, with the recovery date for the test.
Log every impact-tolerance breach with its CRO disposition.
Assess with the Head of Compliance whether any breach warrants proactive BMA communication.
checklist.done: misses and breaches are logged with dispositions and a documented BMA-communication decision.

checklist.step: Preserve the evidence pack per test
actions: File per test: plan, runsheet, contemporaneous timing log, validation outputs, business transaction evidence, debrief and remediation plan.
Apply the 10-year retention label and index by service, application and test date.
Verify a sampled pack opens end-to-end without missing artifacts.
checklist.done: each test has a complete, labelled, retrievable evidence pack.

checklist.step: Refresh scenario severity annually
actions: Review the year's real incidents, threat intelligence from the SOC Lead, and BMA guidance updates.
Retire scenarios the firm passes comfortably twice running and design harder ones.
Document the refresh rationale for the next calendar's approval.
checklist.done: next year's scenarios are demonstrably recalibrated against incidents, threats and guidance.

testing.step: Build the population of required vs executed tests
actions: Export the important-business-service list and CMDB critical-application list as the required-test population.
Export the year's executed test records from ITSM with dates, grades and remediation links.
Reconcile required vs executed; every uncovered service or application is an automatic exception.
testing.done: a reconciled required-vs-executed matrix exists with uncovered items excepted.

testing.step: Verify calendar completeness and timing
actions: Check each executed test fell within the calendar year and each application within 12 months of its prior test.
Confirm the calendar was risk-committee-noted before execution began.
List late or unnoted tests as exceptions.
testing.done: annual-frequency maths holds for every service and application or the miss is excepted.

testing.step: Draw a documented sample of tests
actions: Select 100% of failed tests and tolerance breaches, the claims-payment and policy-administration tests, plus a seeded random selection to reach at least 10 tests.
Include at least one third-party-dependent service test so provider evidence gets inspected.
Record seed, population size and selection date in the workpaper.
testing.done: a reproducible sample covering all fails and key services is documented.

testing.step: Re-perform the grading from raw evidence
actions: Open each sampled test's contemporaneous timing log and recompute recovery time and data-loss window from the raw checkpoints.
Compare to the CMDB RTO/RPO and reach an independent pass/fail before reading the recorded grade.
Any grade that differs from the recomputation, including 'passed by rounding', is an exception.
testing.done: every sampled grade is independently recomputed from raw timings and matches or is excepted.

testing.step: Assess scenario severity against the BMA guidance
actions: Read each sampled scenario against the severe-but-plausible standard and the stated impact tolerance.
Check at least one cyber and one third-party-loss scenario ran in the year.
Flag scenario theatre — walkthroughs graded as exercises, or scenarios identical to comfortably passed prior years.
testing.done: sampled scenarios are judged genuinely severe and the mandatory scenario types are evidenced.

testing.step: Verify evidence-pack integrity
actions: Open each sampled test's pack and confirm plan, runsheet, timing log, validation output, business transaction evidence and debrief are all present.
Check timings were recorded contemporaneously (log timestamps, not a reconstructed table).
Confirm the pack carries the 10-year retention label.
testing.done: every sampled pack is complete, contemporaneous and correctly labelled.

testing.step: Recompute remediation deadline maths
actions: For each sampled debrief, recompute the 30-day clock from debrief date to remediation-plan issue date.
Trace each vulnerability to a closed action with evidence and the required CIO/CRO sign-off, or an open action inside its date.
Confirm failed applications were retested within 90 days and passed.
testing.done: 30-day and 90-day clocks reconcile and every vulnerability traces to an evidenced disposition.

testing.step: Trace results into plans, runbooks and governance
actions: Trace two sampled findings into amended runbook or plan versions with matching change notes.
Verify the annual testing paper reached the risk committee and the minute is filed.
Confirm tolerance breaches show a documented BMA-communication decision.
testing.done: findings trace into documents and governance, and breach-communication decisions are evidenced.

testing.step: Log exceptions with root cause, owner and remediation date
actions: Raise one tracker issue per exception with the service or application, the failure and the resilience exposure.
Assign root cause (calendar slip, evidence gap, grade inflation) and an owner with a cure date.
Carry open exceptions into next year's verification as mandatory retests.
testing.done: every exception has an issue, root cause, owner, cure date and retest commitment.

testing.step: Conclude, sign and report the test
actions: Compute results against the thresholds: 100% coverage, honest grading, 30-day remediation plans.
Write the conclusion (effective / effective with exceptions / ineffective) with evidence references.
Have the independent reviewer, who designed and executed none of the sampled tests, sign the workpaper.
Report to the audit committee and file under Compliance Testing / REG-054 in the compliance evidence repository.
testing.done: a signed workpaper with a stated conclusion and committee reporting is filed.

checklist.step: Define the register schema to the BMA guidance format
actions: Configure the GRC register with the fields the BMA guidance expects: provider legal entity and jurisdiction, service description, start/renewal dates, criticality tier, materiality flag, sub-outsourcing chain, data location, exit strategy reference and contract id.
Add the ICT-specific fields for technology providers: service type (cloud/SaaS/hosting), data classification carried, and the CMDB service id.
Lock materiality and tier fields so only the Third-Party Risk Manager can change them, with change history on.
Publish the field dictionary so every assessor codes vendors the same way.
checklist.done: the register carries every guidance-format field with locked risk fields and a published dictionary.

checklist.step: Register every new vendor within 10 business days of signature
actions: Subscribe to the CLM contract-execution feed so every signed vendor contract raises a GRC intake task automatically.
Complete the register row from the contract: parties, service, term, fees band and the procurement owner.
Route the row to the Third-Party Risk Manager for tiering within the same 10-business-day window.
Reject intake completions with blank mandatory fields rather than registering placeholders.
checklist.done: every executed contract has a complete register row routed for tiering inside 10 business days.

checklist.step: Tier criticality and run the materiality test per vendor
actions: Score each vendor on the tiering matrix: dependence of important business services, substitutability, data sensitivity, and financial exposure.
Apply the BMA materiality test from the outsourcing guidance — could failure of this arrangement materially impair the insurer's operations, service to policyholders or regulatory obligations?
Record the scored rationale on the register row, not just the outcome.
Mark material arrangements with the BMA-notification-required flag, which blocks service commencement until notification evidence is attached.
checklist.done: every vendor carries a scored tier and materiality decision with rationale, and material rows are notification-blocked.

checklist.step: Notify the BMA before any material outsourcing commences
actions: Draft the BMA notification per the guidance: the arrangement, provider, materiality rationale, risk assessment summary, and the oversight and exit arrangements.
Route through Regulatory Counsel for clearance and the Head of Compliance for signature, then send to the BMA supervision team before the service start date.
File the sent notification and any BMA response in the compliance evidence repository and attach them to the register row.
Only then clear the commencement block on the register.
checklist.done: every material arrangement shows a pre-commencement BMA notification filed and attached before its start date.

checklist.step: Complete due diligence proportionate to tier before go-live
actions: For tier-1 vendors collect: financial statements, SOC 2 / ISO 27001 evidence, BCP test summary, sub-outsourcing disclosure, sanctions screening result from the Sanctions Analyst, and data-protection terms reviewed by the Privacy Officer.
For tier-2 collect the reduced pack per the procedure; tier-3 self-attestation.
Store the pack against the register row with an expiry date driven by the tier cadence (tier-1 annual, tier-2 biennial).
Withhold go-live approval until the pack is complete.
checklist.done: each vendor's due-diligence pack matches its tier, is dated, and gated go-live.

checklist.step: Verify the contract carries the BMA-expected clauses
actions: Check each tier-1/material contract in the CLM for: audit and access rights for the insurer and the BMA, termination for cause and convenience, sub-outsourcing consent, data-location and breach-notification duties, and continuity/test-evidence obligations.
Record the clause-check outcome on the register row with the contract section references.
Route clause gaps to Legal Counsel for remediation at the next amendment or renewal, with the gap logged as an exception until cured.
checklist.done: every tier-1/material row shows a clause check with section references, and gaps carry logged remediation paths.

checklist.step: Map vendors to services and applications in the CMDB
actions: Link each ICT vendor's register row to the CMDB services and applications it underpins.
Tag the important business services (from REG-054-C35) that depend on each vendor so criticality flows both ways.
Reconcile quarterly: any CMDB external service without a register row is a completeness failure to fix within 10 business days.
checklist.done: register and CMDB cross-reference completely, with quarterly reconciliation evidence.

checklist.step: Run the concentration and jurisdiction analysis quarterly
actions: Aggregate register rows by ultimate parent, jurisdiction and cloud region to expose concentration on any single provider or geography.
Compare concentrations against the risk-appetite statements approved under Code s.6.
Report breaches of appetite to the Chief Risk Officer with options (diversification, enhanced exit plan, acceptance).
checklist.done: a quarterly concentration analysis exists with appetite comparisons and CRO-routed breaches.

checklist.step: Refresh due diligence on the tier cadence
actions: Work the GRC anniversary queue: re-collect the tier-appropriate pack before each vendor's due-diligence expiry.
Re-run sanctions screening via the Sanctions Analyst and re-check financial health for tier-1 vendors.
Downgrade or exit vendors whose refreshed evidence deteriorates, with the decision minuted on the row.
checklist.done: no tier-1 vendor is past its annual refresh and no tier-2 past biennial, or the overdue row is excepted.

checklist.step: Monitor vendor incidents and performance into the register
actions: Link vendor-caused incidents from ITSM to the vendor's register row automatically by CMDB service id.
Review SLA performance quarterly with the IT Service Delivery Manager for tier-1 ICT vendors.
Reassess the tier of any vendor with repeated severity-1 incidents and record the reassessment.
checklist.done: vendor rows show linked incidents and quarterly SLA reviews, with reassessments recorded where triggered.

checklist.step: Maintain exit strategies for material vendors
actions: Document per material vendor an exit strategy: alternative providers or insourcing route, data-return and deletion steps, transition timeline and trigger conditions.
Review each exit strategy at the vendor's due-diligence refresh.
Reference the exit document on the register row as the BMA guidance format requires.
checklist.done: every material vendor row references a current exit strategy reviewed on cadence.

checklist.step: Attest the register quarterly
actions: Run the quarterly completeness reconciliation: register vs accounts-payable new-vendor spend vs CLM executions vs CMDB external services.
Chase every unmatched vendor to registration or documented out-of-scope rationale within 10 business days.
Sign the quarterly attestation in the GRC platform by the 15th after quarter-end and copy the Compliance Manager for second-line visibility.
checklist.done: a signed quarterly attestation with a clean three-way reconciliation exists by the 15th.

checklist.step: Give the compliance function its monitoring window
actions: Include the third-party register in the compliance monitoring plan per Code s.5/s.6, reviewing a sample of tierings and notifications each half-year.
Report register health, notification compliance and appetite breaches in the compliance report to the board risk committee.
Track committee directions back into the register procedure.
checklist.done: half-yearly second-line reviews and committee reporting on the register are evidenced.

checklist.step: Log and cure register exceptions
actions: Raise a tracker issue for every unregistered vendor, un-notified material arrangement, overdue refresh or clause gap.
Treat an un-notified material arrangement as priority-1: notify the BMA immediately with Regulatory Counsel's input on the late-notification framing.
Record root cause, owner and cure date; CRO signs closure of notification breaches.
checklist.done: every exception is logged with disposition, and notification breaches show immediate BMA correction with CRO sign-off.

checklist.step: Retain register history and evidence
actions: Snapshot the register quarterly into the compliance evidence repository with the 10-year retention label.
Retain terminated-vendor rows with their full due-diligence and notification history for 10 years from termination.
Verify retrieval by vendor name, service and quarter.
checklist.done: quarterly snapshots and terminated-vendor histories are retained and retrievable.

testing.step: Build the population from independent sources
actions: Extract the full register from the GRC platform with tiers, materiality flags and refresh dates.
Independently extract the period's accounts-payable vendor spend, the CLM executed-contract list and the CMDB external-service list.
Normalise vendor names across the four sources before matching.
testing.done: the register and three independent completeness sources are extracted and normalised.

testing.step: Reconcile completeness three ways
actions: Match every AP-paid vendor, executed contract and CMDB external service to a register row.
List every unmatched active vendor as an automatic exception — shadow vendors are the point of this test.
Verify documented out-of-scope rationales for legitimately excluded payees (utilities, tax authorities).
testing.done: every active vendor matches a register row or is excepted, with exclusions rationalised.

testing.step: Draw a documented sample
actions: Take 100% of material arrangements and all vendors added in the period.
Add a seeded random selection of tier-1/tier-2 rows to reach at least 25 vendors.
Record seed, population size and selection date.
testing.done: a reproducible sample covering all material and new vendors is documented.

testing.step: Re-perform tiering and materiality on the sample
actions: Re-score each sampled vendor on the tiering matrix and re-apply the BMA materiality test without reading the recorded outcome first.
Compare conclusions; a vendor the re-performance judges material but the register does not is a critical exception.
Check the recorded rationale is substantive, not a copied template sentence.
testing.done: independent tiering and materiality conclusions are recorded per sampled vendor with differences excepted.

testing.step: Trace BMA notifications for material arrangements
actions: For every material arrangement, locate the filed BMA notification and compare its sent date to the service commencement date.
Confirm counsel clearance and Head of Compliance signature on each notification.
Any commencement preceding notification is a reportable breach, not a documentation gap.
testing.done: every material arrangement shows a pre-commencement, cleared, signed notification or a breach finding.

testing.step: Verify due-diligence cadence maths
actions: Recompute each sampled vendor's refresh due date from its last pack date and tier cadence.
Compare to the actual refresh date and compute the on-cadence rate against the ≥95% threshold.
Open two tier-1 packs and confirm the contents match the procedure's required artifacts, including sanctions screening and privacy review.
testing.done: cadence maths reconciles, the rate is computed, and inspected packs are substantively complete.

testing.step: Verify contract clauses on a sub-sample
actions: Open five sampled material contracts in the CLM and locate the audit/access, termination, sub-outsourcing, data-location and continuity clauses at the recorded section references.
Confirm BMA access rights are explicit, not implied.
List clause gaps without a logged remediation path as exceptions.
testing.done: clause checks re-verify against contract text with unremediated gaps excepted.

testing.step: Test attestation and second-line monitoring discipline
actions: Check a signed register attestation exists for each of the last four quarters, each by the 15th.
Verify the compliance function's half-yearly reviews ran and reached the board risk committee report.
Confirm concentration analyses exist quarterly with CRO routing of appetite breaches.
testing.done: attestations, second-line reviews and concentration analyses are evidenced on schedule.

testing.step: Log exceptions with root cause, owner and remediation date
actions: Raise one tracker issue per exception naming the vendor, the gap and the regulatory exposure.
Assign root cause (intake bypass, mis-tiering, cadence slip) and an owner with a cure date.
Route un-notified material arrangements for immediate BMA correction with Regulatory Counsel.
testing.done: every exception has an issue, root cause, owner and cure date, with notification breaches routed for correction.

testing.step: Conclude, sign and report the test
actions: Compute completeness, notification and cadence results against the thresholds.
Write the conclusion (effective / effective with exceptions / ineffective) with evidence references.
Have the independent reviewer, who maintains no register row, sign the workpaper.
Report to the audit committee and file under Compliance Testing / REG-054.
testing.done: a signed workpaper with a stated conclusion and committee reporting is filed.
