In-scope systems.value: Incident records and reporting-clock timestamps in ServiceNow ITSM; detection telemetry in the SIEM; BMA correspondence filed to the compliance evidence repository

Compliance procedure documented.value: Regulatory Incident Reporting Runbook — reporting-event criteria, classification within 24 hours of detection, initial BMA notification without undue delay (72-hour internal standard), full report within 14 days of the initial notification, and the drafting/clearance chain

Compliance procedure approved.value: Approved by the Chief Info Security Officer and the Chief Risk Officer; reviewed annually and after every reportable incident

Filing/reporting deadlines tracked.value: Event-driven — classification within 24 hours of detection; initial BMA notification within the 72-hour internal standard of determining a reporting event; full written report within 14 days of the initial notification; remediation-completion update as committed in that report

Deadline reminders configured.value: ITSM auto-starts the reporting clock when severity 1-2 is set: alerts at classification+12h, notification T-24h/T-8h, and full-report T-7/T-3/T-1 days across the 14-day window

Evidence retained per the retention requ.value: Incident timelines, classification decisions, BMA notifications and reports, and remediation evidence retained 10 years from incident closure in the compliance evidence repository

Violations/exceptions logged with dispos.value: Any late classification, notification past the 72-hour standard, full report past 14 days, or reportable event found unreported in the back-test is logged with disposition and a BMA-communication record

Remediation sign-off captured.value: CISO signs closure of cyber-incident reporting failures; the Chief Risk Officer signs operational-incident reporting failures

Test population (in-scope transactions,.value: All severity 1-3 incidents in ITSM for the trailing 12 months, all SIEM major-alert cases, and all BMA incident notifications and reports sent in the period

Pass/fail thresholds.value: 100% of reportable events notified within the 72-hour standard and fully reported within 14 days of initial notification; zero reportable events discovered in the back-test that were never reported — one such finding is an automatic fail

Compliance test frequency matched to the.value: Obligation is event-driven; test annually over the trailing 12 months, plus a classification back-test each half-year

Independent reviewer (segregated from th.value: Reviewer must not have handled or classified any sampled incident

Evidence location for test results.value: Annual incident-reporting test workpaper in the compliance evidence repository under Compliance Testing / REG-054, referencing ITSM incident ids

Regulator-ready documentation.value: Per reportable incident: the timeline, classification record, initial notification, 14-day report and remediation updates as one indexed pack, producible to the BMA within 5 business days

Regulator response path.value: Incident Response Lead drafts notifications and reports; Regulatory Counsel clears; the Chief Info Security Officer (cyber) or Chief Risk Officer (operational) signs; the Head of Compliance sends to the BMA supervision team

checklist.step: Codify the reporting-event criteria into the incident process
actions: Translate the Cyber Code's reporting-event definition into concrete triggers: material policyholder-service disruption, data breach affecting policyholder information, important-business-service outage beyond tolerance, ransomware or destructive attack, and material third-party incidents inherited from the REG-054-C37 register.
Build the triggers into the ITSM severity matrix so severity 1-2 automatically raises a 'regulatory assessment required' task.
Configure the ITSM record to timestamp detection, classification, determination, notification and report events immutably.
Publish the criteria card to the SOC and the major-incident bridge roster.
checklist.done: reporting-event triggers are wired into ITSM severities with immutable clock timestamps and a published criteria card.

checklist.step: Classify every major incident within 24 hours of detection
actions: On every severity 1-2 incident, complete the regulatory assessment task: apply the criteria card and record reportable / not reportable / monitoring with the reasoning verbatim.
Consult the Operational Risk Manager on operational (non-cyber) incidents before concluding.
Record the determination timestamp — this starts the notification clock for reportable events.
Re-assess at every material change in impact and log each re-assessment; incidents grow, and so does reportability.
checklist.done: every severity 1-2 incident carries a reasoned, timestamped regulatory determination within 24 hours, re-assessed on impact changes.

checklist.step: Escalate through the three lines the moment an event is reportable
actions: Notify the Chief Info Security Officer (cyber) or Chief Risk Officer (operational), the Head of Compliance and Regulatory Counsel within 2 hours of the reportable determination.
Convene the regulatory-reporting cell as a distinct thread from the technical bridge so report accuracy never competes with restoration.
Brief the Chief Executive Officer for incidents with policyholder-facing impact.
Minute the escalation times in the ITSM record.
checklist.done: the escalation chain is executed and minuted within 2 hours of determination, with a distinct reporting cell running.

checklist.step: Send the initial BMA notification within the 72-hour standard
actions: Draft the initial notification on the runbook template: what happened, when detected, services and policyholder impact, containment status, and the named incident contact.
State facts known at the time and label estimates as estimates — the 14-day report carries the detail; never delay notification to perfect it.
Route through Regulatory Counsel for clearance and the CISO/CRO for signature, then the Head of Compliance sends it to the BMA supervision team within 72 hours of the reportable determination.
File the sent notification with its delivery confirmation and log the sent timestamp in ITSM.
checklist.done: a cleared, signed initial notification is with the BMA inside 72 hours of determination, filed with its timestamp.

checklist.step: Notify parallel authorities where the incident triggers them
actions: Assess whether the incident is also a PIPA breach requiring notification to the Privacy Commissioner and affected individuals (feeds the REG-054 privacy obligations).
Coordinate with the Financial Crime AML Officer where the incident involves fraud or sanctioned actors.
Keep the BMA report and any other filings factually consistent — one master timeline, many extracts.
Log each parallel notification decision with its rationale.
checklist.done: parallel notification decisions are logged with rationale and all filings draw from one master timeline.

checklist.step: Build and hold the master incident timeline
actions: Assemble the timeline from SIEM telemetry, ITSM entries and bridge notes: detection, escalations, containment actions, impact milestones and recovery, each with source references.
Update it daily during the incident and freeze a copy at notification and at report submission.
Preserve the underlying logs under legal hold when Regulatory Counsel directs.
checklist.done: a source-referenced master timeline exists with frozen copies at each filing point and holds applied on direction.

checklist.step: Deliver the full written report within 14 days of the initial notification
actions: Draft the full report per the Cyber Code: root cause, attack vector or failure mode, data and policyholder impact quantified, containment and recovery actions with timings, third-party involvement, and the remediation plan with dates.
Reconcile every fact against the frozen timeline and the initial notification, explaining any corrected early estimate.
Clear through Regulatory Counsel, obtain CISO/CRO signature, and have the Head of Compliance deliver it within 14 days of the initial notification.
If a material fact cannot be confirmed inside 14 days, deliver the report on time with the open item flagged and a committed supplement date — never blow the deadline for completeness.
File the report and delivery confirmation, and record the sent timestamp in ITSM.
checklist.done: the full report is with the BMA within 14 days of initial notification, timeline-reconciled, with any open items flagged and dated.

checklist.step: Answer BMA follow-up questions within 14 days of each request
actions: Log every BMA follow-up question on the incident with its received date and a 14-day response target.
Source answers from the master timeline and the incident engineers, cleared through Regulatory Counsel.
File each response against the incident pack and close the log entry with the sent date.
checklist.done: every BMA follow-up shows a logged, cleared response within 14 days of the request.

checklist.step: Report remediation completion as committed
actions: Track the remediation actions committed in the full report through the ITSM problem record to closure with evidence.
Send the BMA the completion update on the date committed in the report, or a pre-deadline extension letter if a date will slip.
Have the CISO or CRO sign the completion update.
checklist.done: committed remediation updates reach the BMA on their committed dates with evidence-backed closures.

checklist.step: Run the post-incident review within 20 business days of closure
actions: Review both the incident and the reporting performance: was classification honest, were the 72-hour and 14-day clocks met, did clearance add delay?
Feed control gaps into the resilience test scenarios (REG-054-C36) and plan updates (REG-054-C35).
Update the runbook with any reporting-process fix and re-issue it.
checklist.done: a post-incident review covering reporting performance exists with fixes fed into scenarios, plans and the runbook.

checklist.step: Back-test monthly for reportable events that slipped through
actions: Review all severity 2-3 incidents closed in the month against the criteria card, looking for events wrongly classified as non-reportable.
Check SIEM major-alert cases that never became ITSM incidents.
Escalate any missed reportable event to the Head of Compliance the same day for a late-notification decision with Regulatory Counsel.
checklist.done: a monthly back-test record exists and any missed event shows a same-day escalation and disposition.

checklist.step: Drill the reporting chain twice a year
actions: Run a timed drill from simulated detection to a draft initial notification, including counsel clearance and signature steps.
Verify the out-of-hours path: on-call rosters for counsel, CISO and Head of Compliance reachable within 2 hours.
Debrief and fix any step that consumed disproportionate clock time.
checklist.done: two timed drills per year show the chain producing a clearable notification inside the 72-hour standard.

checklist.step: Train incident handlers on the reporting duty
actions: Assign the annual regulatory-reporting module to the SOC, major-incident managers and service-desk escalation staff.
Include the criteria card and the rule that classification doubt escalates to the Incident Response Lead, never resolves silently to non-reportable.
Track completion and chase past 30 days.
checklist.done: LMS records show current training for every incident-handling role.

checklist.step: Log reporting failures as exceptions with BMA-facing disposition
actions: Raise a tracker issue for any late classification, late notification, late report or back-test miss.
Decide with Regulatory Counsel whether proactive disclosure of the failure to the BMA is required, and record the decision.
Obtain CISO or CRO sign-off on closure per the incident type.
checklist.done: every reporting failure carries an issue, a disclosure decision and the required executive sign-off.

checklist.step: Retain the complete incident-reporting record
actions: Assemble per reportable incident one indexed pack: timeline, determinations, notifications, full report, follow-ups and remediation updates.
Apply the 10-year retention label and index by incident id and date.
Verify a sampled pack opens complete.
checklist.done: every reportable incident has one complete, labelled, retrievable pack.

testing.step: Build the population from ITSM and SIEM, not the reporting log
actions: Extract all severity 1-3 incidents for the trailing 12 months with their timestamps.
Extract SIEM major-alert cases and reconcile them to ITSM incidents, listing alerts that never became incidents.
Extract the list of BMA notifications and reports sent in the period from the correspondence files.
testing.done: incident, alert and filing populations are extracted and reconciled in the workpaper.

testing.step: Re-perform classification on the full severity 1-2 set
actions: Apply the criteria card independently to every severity 1-2 incident before reading the recorded determination.
Compare conclusions; an incident the re-performance judges reportable but the record does not is an automatic fail candidate.
Check every determination was made within 24 hours of detection and carries substantive reasoning.
testing.done: independent classifications exist for all severity 1-2 incidents with differences and late determinations excepted.

testing.step: Draw the deadline-testing sample
actions: Take 100% of reportable incidents in the period.
Add a seeded random 15 severity-3 incidents to test for under-classification at the boundary.
Record seed, population and selection date.
testing.done: all reportable incidents plus a reproducible boundary sample are documented.

testing.step: Recompute the notification clock per reportable incident
actions: Recompute elapsed time from the reportable-determination timestamp to the notification sent timestamp against the 72-hour standard.
Verify the timestamps are system-generated in ITSM, not typed into a summary afterwards.
Flag any determination timestamp suspiciously later than the impact evidence in the timeline — clock-starting games are the classic failure.
testing.done: notification elapsed times are recomputed from immutable timestamps with clock-integrity checks noted.

testing.step: Recompute the 14-day report clock and reconcile content
actions: Recompute days from initial notification to full-report delivery against the 14-day requirement for every reportable incident.
Reconcile three facts per report (root cause, impact figures, remediation dates) against the frozen master timeline.
Check flagged open items received their committed supplements on time.
testing.done: 14-day maths holds for every report, content reconciles to the timeline, and supplements arrived as committed.

testing.step: Verify the clearance and signature chain
actions: Confirm each notification and report shows Regulatory Counsel clearance and the correct CISO/CRO signature before sending.
Confirm the Head of Compliance sent each filing to the named BMA contact with delivery confirmation on file.
List any filing sent outside the chain as an exception.
testing.done: every filing evidences the full clearance, signature and delivery chain.

testing.step: Test back-tests, drills and follow-up timeliness
actions: Check twelve monthly back-test records exist and re-perform one month's back-test in full.
Verify two timed drills ran in the year and their fixes were applied to the runbook.
Recompute the 14-day clock on every BMA follow-up response in the period.
testing.done: back-tests, drills and follow-up responses all verify on schedule with one back-test re-performed.

testing.step: Trace remediation commitments to closure
actions: For each reportable incident, trace the report's remediation commitments to closed problem-record actions with evidence.
Compare completion-update sent dates to the dates committed in the report.
List silent slips as exceptions with disclosure-assessment flags.
testing.done: every commitment traces to evidenced closure and an on-time BMA update, or is excepted.

testing.step: Log exceptions with root cause, owner and remediation date
actions: Raise one tracker issue per exception with the incident id, the clock or classification failure and the supervisory exposure.
Assign root cause (late determination, clearance drag, criteria ambiguity) and an owner with a cure date.
Route unreported reportable events for immediate disclosure assessment with Regulatory Counsel.
testing.done: every exception has an issue, root cause, owner, cure date, and misses carry disclosure assessments.

testing.step: Conclude, sign and report the test
actions: Compute results against the thresholds: 100% timely notification and reporting, zero unreported events.
Write the conclusion (effective / effective with exceptions / ineffective) with evidence references.
Have the independent reviewer, who handled no sampled incident, sign the workpaper.
Report to the audit committee and the Chief Info Security Officer, and file under Compliance Testing / REG-054.
testing.done: a signed workpaper with a stated conclusion and committee reporting is filed.

checklist.step: Maintain the list inventory and 24-hour update SLA
actions: Subscribe the screening engine to the UK consolidated list as extended to Bermuda, the UN consolidated list, and the OFAC SDN and non-SDN lists for USD-touching business.
Verify each list version loads within 24 hours of publication by comparing the engine's list-version screen to the publisher's site, and log the load time daily.
Reconcile record counts per list after each load and investigate any drop against the prior version.
Escalate a feed older than 24 hours to the Financial Crime AML Officer immediately.
checklist.done: the daily log shows every list current within 24 hours with reconciled record counts.

checklist.step: Wire pre-bind screening into the policy issuance gate
actions: Feed applicant, policyholder, beneficial-owner and named-insured parties from the Policy Administration Platform to the screening engine at submission and at any party change.
Configure the bind transaction to hard-block until a screening result of clear or false-positive-dispositioned is returned — no user override role exists.
Ensure beneficial owners above the 25% threshold from the KYC file are included as screened parties, pulled from the AML programme records (REG-054-C40).
Test the block quarterly by attempting to bind a case with an open alert in a test environment.
checklist.done: bind is technically impossible without a screening result and the quarterly block test passes.

checklist.step: Screen payments before release
actions: Route claim payments, premium refunds and commission payments through the screening engine before the Payment Gateway releases funds, screening payee name, bank country and any intermediary.
Hold any payment with an open alert in a pended queue invisible to ordinary payment operators.
Reconcile daily that released-payment count equals screened-clear count; any unexplained difference is a same-day escalation.
checklist.done: the daily reconciliation shows every released payment carried a clear screening result.

checklist.step: Rescreen the in-force book on every list update
actions: Run the delta batch rescreen of all in-force parties within 24 hours of each list update, and a full-book rescreen monthly as a safety net.
Verify the batch completion report shows 100% of the party file processed; rerun failures the same day.
File the batch completion reports as the ongoing-screening evidence.
checklist.done: delta rescreens follow every list update and monthly full-book runs complete at 100%, evidenced by filed reports.

checklist.step: Tune and document match thresholds annually
actions: Run the annual threshold-tuning exercise with sample data: measure detection of seeded true names and variants (transliterations, initials, transposed name parts) against false-positive volume.
Document the chosen fuzzy-match thresholds per party type with the tuning evidence — an undocumented threshold is indefensible at exam.
Have the Head of Compliance approve the tuned configuration before deployment, and version the config change.
checklist.done: current thresholds trace to a dated, approved tuning exercise with seeded-detection evidence.

checklist.step: Adjudicate alerts four-eyes within SLA
actions: Work each alert in the case manager: compare name, DOB, nationality, address and identifiers against the list entry, and record the discounting rationale field-by-field.
Disposition false positives with a second reviewer's concurrence — no single-handed closes.
Escalate possible true matches to the Financial Crime AML Officer within 4 business hours with the evidence attached.
Clear alerts within 24 hours for pre-bind and payment queues, 48 hours for batch queues.
checklist.done: every alert shows field-level rationale, a second reviewer, SLA-compliant timing and escalated potentials.

checklist.step: Freeze on confirmation and stop all dealings
actions: On a confirmed match, immediately flag the policy in the Policy Administration Platform to block payments, surrenders, loans and endorsements, and block the payee in the Payment Gateway.
Instruct Claims and Policy Service in writing that no funds or economic benefit may pass to the designated party.
Convene Regulatory Counsel the same day on licence-application options and policyholder-communication constraints.
Record the freeze time, scope and instructed teams in the case record.
checklist.done: confirmed matches show same-day system blocks, written stop instructions and a counsel consult, all timestamped.

checklist.step: Report freezes to the FSIU and OFAC where applicable
actions: Report the frozen asset or rejected transaction to Bermuda's Financial Sanctions Implementation Unit without delay, using the FSIU's compliance reporting form with the designation reference, asset description and value.
Where OFAC jurisdiction attaches (US person, USD clearing), file the blocked-property report via the OFAC Reporting System within 10 business days of blocking.
File copies of each report and acknowledgement in the compliance evidence repository against the case id.
Diarise the OFAC annual blocked-property report (due by September 30) if any property remains blocked.
checklist.done: every freeze shows an FSIU report, an OFAC report where applicable within 10 business days, and filed acknowledgements.

checklist.step: Screen third parties and reinsurers via the vendor and treaty processes
actions: Screen counterparties from the third-party register (REG-054-C37) at onboarding and on the batch cycle.
Screen reinsurers, brokers and coverholders from the treaty and producer records before contract inception.
Return results to the owning process with the same clear/blocked discipline as policyholder screening.
checklist.done: vendor, reinsurer and intermediary populations flow through the same screening and evidence discipline.

checklist.step: Monitor screening-feed completeness
actions: Reconcile monthly the party counts sent to the engine against source counts in the Policy Administration Platform and Payment Gateway.
Investigate any source table or product line missing from the feed — new products are the classic gap.
Sign the monthly completeness reconciliation and file it.
checklist.done: monthly reconciliations prove every party source reaches the engine, with gaps investigated and signed off.

checklist.step: Run quarterly seeded-name detection checks
actions: Inject test parties matching current list entries (exact and variant spellings) into a controlled screening run each quarter.
Confirm every seed alerts at or above the tuned threshold; a missed seed halts and triggers immediate threshold review.
Record seeds, results and any corrective tuning in the quarterly check log.
checklist.done: quarterly seed checks show 100% detection or a documented halt-and-retune.

checklist.step: Train underwriting, claims and payments staff on sanctions red flags
actions: Assign the annual sanctions module to underwriters, claims examiners, payment operators and producer-facing staff.
Cover the no-override rule, red flags (payee changes to third countries, unusual beneficiary substitutions) and the escalation route.
Track completion and report laggards past 30 days to their managers.
checklist.done: LMS records show current sanctions training across the exposed functions.

checklist.step: Report screening health to governance
actions: Report quarterly to the board risk committee: alert volumes, SLA performance, list latency, freezes and regulator filings, seed-check results.
Table threshold changes and resource needs for decision.
Minute directions and track them to closure.
checklist.done: quarterly governance reporting on screening health is tabled and minuted.

checklist.step: Log and cure screening exceptions
actions: Raise a tracker issue for every bind without screening, late list load, SLA breach or payment released against an open alert.
For a payment that reached a designated party, invoke the freeze-and-report steps retroactively and record the FSIU disclosure decision with Regulatory Counsel.
Assign root cause and owner; the Head of Compliance signs closures.
checklist.done: every exception is logged with disposition, and any funds-to-designated-party event shows a regulator disclosure decision.

checklist.step: Retain screening evidence per the record-keeping rules
actions: Archive screening logs, alert dispositions with reviewer identities, batch reports and freeze cases with the 5-year label (10 years for freeze cases).
Verify a sampled case retrieves with its full field-level rationale intact.
Confirm engine log purges never run ahead of the retention schedule.
checklist.done: screening records are retained on schedule and sampled cases retrieve complete.

testing.step: Build the bound-policy and payment populations from source systems
actions: Extract all policies bound in the trailing 12 months from the Policy Administration Platform and all released payments from the Payment Gateway.
Extract the screening engine's result log for the same period.
Reconcile counts between source systems and the screening log before sampling.
testing.done: bound, paid and screened populations are extracted and count-reconciled.

testing.step: Test the pre-bind gate on 100% match basis
actions: Match every bound policy to a screening result timestamped before its bind timestamp.
List any bind without a prior result as an automatic exception — no sampling on this control.
Attempt a test-environment bind with an open alert to prove the block still holds.
testing.done: every bind shows a prior screening result and the block test passes.

testing.step: Sample payments and rescreens
actions: Draw a seeded random sample of 30 released payments and verify each carried a clear result before release.
Verify batch rescreens followed each of five sampled list-update dates within 24 hours, from the batch completion reports.
Record seed, populations and selection dates.
testing.done: sampled payments show pre-release clears and sampled list updates show timely rescreens.

testing.step: Recompute list-load latency
actions: For ten sampled list publications across UK/UN/OFAC sources, compare publisher publication timestamps to engine load timestamps.
Recompute the 24-hour SLA on each and flag breaches.
Check the daily latency log recorded the same values.
testing.done: load-latency recomputation reconciles to the log with breaches flagged.

testing.step: Re-perform alert adjudications
actions: Draw 25 dispositioned alerts including all escalated potentials, and re-adjudicate each against the list entry without reading the analyst's rationale first.
Compare conclusions; any false positive the re-performance judges a possible match is a critical exception.
Verify four-eyes evidence and SLA timing on every sampled alert.
testing.done: independent re-adjudications match recorded dispositions, with four-eyes and SLA verified or excepted.

testing.step: Run an independent seeded-detection test
actions: Inject auditor-chosen seed names (exact, transliterated, transposed) into a controlled run without telling the screening team the variants.
Confirm 100% detection at the tuned thresholds; a missed seed is an automatic fail.
Compare results against the team's own quarterly seed checks for consistency.
testing.done: the independent seed test detects every variant or the fail is recorded.

testing.step: Trace freeze cases to FSIU/OFAC reports
actions: For every confirmed match in the period, trace the same-day system blocks, the FSIU report and, where applicable, the OFAC blocked-property report within 10 business days.
Verify no payment, surrender or benefit passed after the freeze timestamp by querying the Payment Gateway and policy transaction history.
Check acknowledgements are filed against each case.
testing.done: every freeze traces to timely reports and a provably clean post-freeze transaction history.

testing.step: Verify feed completeness independently
actions: Independently list party-bearing sources (new products, payment types, reinsurer/vendor populations) and confirm each feeds the engine.
Re-perform one monthly completeness reconciliation from raw counts.
List any unscreened source as a critical exception.
testing.done: all party sources are proven to reach the engine or the gap is excepted as critical.

testing.step: Log exceptions with root cause, owner and remediation date
actions: Raise one tracker issue per exception with the party or payment id, the control that failed and the sanctions exposure.
Assign root cause (feed gap, threshold miss, SLA overload) and an owner with a cure date.
Route any funds-to-designated-party finding for immediate FSIU disclosure assessment with Regulatory Counsel.
testing.done: every exception has an issue, root cause, owner, cure date, and critical findings carry disclosure assessments.

testing.step: Conclude, sign and report the test
actions: Compute results against the thresholds: 100% pre-bind and pre-payment coverage, zero unfrozen matches, full seed detection.
Write the conclusion (effective / effective with exceptions / ineffective) with evidence references.
Have the independent reviewer, who adjudicated no sampled alert, sign the workpaper.
Report to the audit committee and the Head of Compliance, and file under Compliance Testing / REG-054.
testing.done: a signed workpaper with a stated conclusion and committee reporting is filed.

checklist.step: Maintain the MLRO designation and mandate
actions: Hold a current board resolution appointing the MLRO and a named deputy, with the mandate: unrestricted access to CDD and transaction records, direct board reporting line, and sole authority over SAR decisions.
Notify the BMA of any change of MLRO through the supervision team per the notification expectations, filing the correspondence.
Record the designation, deputy and mandate in the GRC programme record and re-verify at each annual cycle.
Confirm the role's independence — the MLRO must not own the sales or distribution targets for the covered products.
checklist.done: a current board-resolved MLRO and deputy exist with a filed mandate and BMA notification history.

checklist.step: Refresh the business risk assessment annually
actions: Assess ML/TF risk across the covered products: single-premium and top-up features, surrender values, assignments, third-party payments, non-resident customers and intermediary channels.
Weigh Bermuda national risk assessment findings and FATF/typology updates for life insurance.
Rate inherent risk, map controls, conclude residual risk and set the year's mitigation actions.
Present to the board for approval with the programme manual and file the minute.
checklist.done: a board-approved business risk assessment dated within 12 months drives the year's mitigation actions.

checklist.step: Keep the programme manual current and board-approved
actions: Update the AML/ATF Programme Manual for regulation changes, BMA guidance-note revisions and the refreshed risk assessment.
Version the manual in the GRC document module with a change summary.
Obtain board re-approval within 12 months of the prior approval and record the minute reference on the programme record.
checklist.done: the manual's current version carries a board approval minute dated within 12 months.

checklist.step: Enforce risk-rated CDD before covered-policy issue
actions: At new business, collect and verify identity for the policyholder, payer where different, and beneficial owners above 25%, using the standards in the manual.
Score customer risk (residency, PEP status via the screening feed, channel, product features, premium size) and record the rating on the policy record.
Apply EDD to high-risk and PEP cases: senior-management approval to proceed, source-of-funds and source-of-wealth evidence for single premiums above the manual's threshold.
Block policy issue in the Policy Administration Platform until CDD status is complete — mirroring the sanctions pre-bind gate (REG-054-C39).
Coordinate data handling with the Privacy Officer so CDD collection stays within PIPA lawful-use grounds.
checklist.done: no covered policy issues without complete, risk-rated CDD, with EDD evidence on every high-risk and PEP case.

checklist.step: Re-verify CDD at trigger events
actions: Define trigger events in Actimize: ownership assignment, beneficiary change, payer change, large top-up, early surrender, and address moves to higher-risk jurisdictions.
Route triggered policies to the CDD refresh queue with a 20-business-day completion target.
Refresh high-risk customers on the periodic cycle set in the manual regardless of triggers.
Escalate refreshes that stall past target to the Financial Crime AML Officer.
checklist.done: trigger and periodic refreshes run to target with stalls escalated, evidenced in the queue records.

checklist.step: Run transaction monitoring tuned to insurance typologies
actions: Operate scenarios for the covered products: early surrender after single premium, premium overpayment with refund request, third-party premium payments, rapid assignment chains, and structuring below the source-of-funds threshold.
Review alerts within the 5/10-business-day SLAs, documenting the disposition rationale per alert.
Verify monthly that every scenario executed against complete data — a silent scenario month is an exception.
Re-tune thresholds annually with documented before/after detection evidence.
checklist.done: scenarios run monthly-verified and alerts close within SLA with documented rationale and annual tuning evidence.

checklist.step: Operate the internal suspicion-reporting channel
actions: Maintain the internal report form and route by which any employee reports suspicion directly to the MLRO, bypassing line management.
Log every internal report on receipt in the restricted SAR register with its date and reporter function.
Assess each report without delay, documenting the decision to file or not file with reasons — the not-filed rationale matters as much as the filed one.
Protect reporters from tipping-off risk: no feedback beyond acknowledgement.
checklist.done: every internal report shows a logged receipt and a reasoned, dated MLRO decision in the restricted register.

checklist.step: File SARs with the Financial Intelligence Agency
actions: File each SAR through the FIA's goAML portal as soon as practicable after suspicion forms, completing the subject, transaction and grounds-for-suspicion sections in full.
Record the goAML reference and filing date in the restricted register; retain the filed copy under the SAR confidentiality wall.
Apply post-SAR handling: consent requests before proceeding with implicated transactions where the Regulations require, and strict tipping-off controls on customer contact.
Track FIA follow-up requests to response in the restricted register.
checklist.done: every filed SAR shows a goAML reference, walled records, consent handling where required and closed FIA follow-ups.

checklist.step: Screen and oversee intermediaries selling covered products
actions: Verify each broker or producer channel's own AML arrangements before relying on them for any CDD element, documenting the reliance decision per the Regulations' reliance conditions.
Retest reliance annually and on any adverse indicator from complaints or monitoring.
Keep the responsibility split written into producer agreements — reliance never transfers the insurer's liability.
checklist.done: every reliance arrangement is documented, conditioned and annually retested.

checklist.step: Deliver risk-based AML training
actions: Assign annual AML/ATF training in the learning management system: all staff baseline, enhanced modules for new business, claims, surrenders and payments teams, and MLRO-specialist training.
Include insurance-specific typologies and the internal reporting route in the enhanced modules.
Train new joiners in exposed roles within 30 days of start.
Report completion to the Financial Crime AML Officer monthly and chase past-due learners.
checklist.done: training completion is ≥95% with exposed-role and new-joiner coverage evidenced in LMS records.

checklist.step: Keep AML records to the retention standard
actions: Retain CDD files and transaction records at least 5 years from relationship end, and SAR materials in the walled store with MLRO-chain-only access.
Verify retrieval of a sampled CDD file within 2 business days — the Regulations expect records producible promptly to authorities.
Confirm PIPA retention-minimisation decisions never delete records inside the AML retention floor.
checklist.done: retention floors are enforced, SAR walls hold, and sampled records retrieve within 2 business days.

checklist.step: Deliver the MLRO annual report to the board
actions: Write the annual MLRO report: programme health, CDD and monitoring statistics, internal reports and SAR volumes (aggregated, not case detail), training coverage, regulatory developments and resource adequacy.
Table it at the board via the board portal and minute the discussion and directions.
File the report and minute as core exam evidence.
checklist.done: the MLRO annual report is tabled, minuted and filed within the annual cycle.

checklist.step: Commission the independent AML audit
actions: Schedule the independent audit of the AML/ATF programme per the Regulations' independent-test expectation, scoped to CDD, monitoring, reporting and governance.
Ensure the audit team is independent of the MLRO function.
Track findings into the remediation process with Head of Compliance sign-off (CRO sign-off for findings on the MLRO function itself).
checklist.done: an independent audit ran in cycle and its findings are tracked with segregated sign-offs.

checklist.step: Log and cure programme exceptions
actions: Raise a tracker issue for every policy issued on incomplete CDD, silent scenario period, late assessment or training lapse — keeping SAR case detail out of the general tracker.
Assign root cause and owner with a cure date proportionate to exposure.
Report exception themes in the MLRO annual report.
checklist.done: exceptions are logged with dispositions, SAR confidentiality intact, and themes reach the annual report.

checklist.step: Track BMA AML supervision and fold in findings
actions: Log BMA AML/ATF questionnaires, onsite visit requests and findings through the correspondence log (REG-054-C33) and remediation process (REG-054-C34).
Update the programme manual and risk assessment for each accepted finding.
Evidence the closure trail per finding.
checklist.done: BMA AML supervision items flow through logged correspondence, remediation and manual updates.

testing.step: Build the population of covered policies, alerts and reports
actions: Extract all covered life & annuity policies issued in the trailing 12 months from the Policy Administration Platform.
Extract Actimize alert and case volumes, the CDD refresh queue and, via the MLRO under confidentiality, the counts from the restricted SAR register.
Reconcile issued-policy counts to new-business reports before sampling.
testing.done: policy, alert, refresh and (walled) reporting populations are extracted and reconciled.

testing.step: Verify the designation, approvals and annual-cycle dates
actions: Sight the board resolution appointing the MLRO and deputy, and the BMA notification of the current holder.
Recompute the 12-month clocks: manual approval, business risk assessment approval and MLRO annual report against their prior dates.
A lapsed designation or approval past 12 months is an automatic fail.
testing.done: designation and all annual-cycle approvals verify inside 12 months, or the fail is recorded.

testing.step: Draw the CDD sample
actions: Select 100% of PEP and high-risk-rated policies issued in the period plus a seeded random selection of standard-risk policies to reach at least 30 files.
Include at least five single-premium cases above the source-of-funds threshold.
Record seed, population size and selection date.
testing.done: a reproducible sample covering all PEP/high-risk and threshold single-premium cases is documented.

testing.step: Re-perform CDD on each sampled file
actions: Open each file and verify identity evidence, beneficial-owner coverage above 25%, and a risk rating recorded before the issue date.
Re-score the customer risk from the file facts and compare to the recorded rating.
For EDD cases, verify senior-management approval and source-of-funds/wealth evidence that actually explains the money, not a form asserting it.
Confirm the issue timestamp post-dates CDD completion.
testing.done: every sampled file shows complete pre-issue CDD with defensible ratings and substantive EDD, or is excepted.

testing.step: Verify monitoring coverage and re-perform alert handling
actions: Check the monthly scenario-execution logs for the year and flag any silent scenario period.
Re-adjudicate 20 sampled closed alerts against the transaction data without reading the analyst rationale first.
Compare conclusions and verify SLA timing; a closure the re-performance judges suspicious is a critical exception.
Sight the annual tuning evidence behind current thresholds.
testing.done: scenario coverage is continuous, sampled closures withstand re-performance, and tuning is evidenced.

testing.step: Test the internal-report-to-SAR chain under confidentiality
actions: With MLRO-supervised access, trace every internal suspicion report in the period to a dated, reasoned file/no-file decision.
For filed SARs, verify a goAML reference exists and follow-ups closed, without copying case content into the workpaper.
Verify not-filed decisions carry substantive reasoning.
Confirm tipping-off controls: no evidence of customer or line-management disclosure.
testing.done: the full chain from internal report to decision and filing verifies under the confidentiality wall.

testing.step: Recompute refresh and training maths
actions: Recompute the 20-business-day clock on ten sampled trigger-event CDD refreshes.
Recompute training completion rates from LMS raw data against the ≥95% threshold and check exposed-role and 30-day new-joiner coverage.
Verify periodic high-risk refreshes ran on the manual's cycle.
testing.done: refresh clocks, training rates and periodic-review cycles reconcile from raw data.

testing.step: Test record retention and retrieval
actions: Request three closed-relationship CDD files and time retrieval against the 2-business-day standard.
Verify the 5-year retention floor held against any PIPA minimisation deletions.
Confirm SAR-store access logs show MLRO-chain-only access.
testing.done: retrievals meet the standard, retention floors held and SAR access logs are clean.

testing.step: Log exceptions with root cause, owner and remediation date
actions: Raise one tracker issue per exception with the policy or process affected and the ML/TF exposure, keeping SAR detail walled.
Assign root cause (gate bypass, rating drift, scenario outage) and an owner with a cure date.
Route findings about the MLRO function to the Chief Risk Officer for segregated sign-off.
testing.done: every exception has an issue, root cause, owner and cure date with segregation preserved.

testing.step: Conclude, sign and report the test
actions: Compute results against the thresholds: 100% pre-issue CDD, 100% assessed internal reports, in-cycle approvals, ≥95% training.
Write the conclusion (effective / effective with exceptions / ineffective) with evidence references, satisfying the Regulations' independent-audit expectation.
Have the independent reviewer, outside the MLRO function, sign the workpaper.
Report to the audit committee and board, and file under Compliance Testing / REG-054 with SAR sections access-restricted.
testing.done: a signed workpaper with a stated conclusion, committee reporting and walled SAR sections is filed.
